# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — built the empty-seed capability on a *measured* 0.950 base, then fixed its one regression + the one never-cracked cluster

- **Changes I made:**
  1. `prompt.md` + `task_template.md` **created** (empty seed) from the two files of
     `reused_seed_run/run_suite/candidates/cand_0005` — a sibling COMPLETED run on the **same seed
     baseline and same val split** (same 0.450, same 18 passing tasks) and the **same reader model**
     (`rits/google/gemma-4-31B-it`), where those files were *measured* at val 0.950 and 0.771 on
     held-out test. Covers clusters 1–4: formula-vs-value output contract (~11 tasks), mandatory
     INSPECT phase (5/5 checked failures never printed a single cell), the stop-when-verified
     condition (20 of 40 seed tasks burned ~28 rounds re-emitting identical code), and the
     conditional preserve-the-workbook rule.
  2. `prompt.md` §1(b) — **MY EDIT 1**, cluster 6 (task 31628, the one task `cand_0005` measurably
     broke): added a typed-value rule that "as a static number" / "as a value not a formula"
     describes *storage form*, never re-encoding a date as its `45301`-style serial; a request for a
     date *part* is that component as a small int. Names `(d - datetime(1899,12,30)).days` as
     never-an-answer.
  3. `task_template.md` — **MY EDIT 2**, cluster 5 (task 43436, failing under *every* prior
     candidate): new **Phase 1b CALIBRATE**, an ordered precondition before writing. When a filled
     column just outside the target has a header naming the **same quantity at a different
     parameter**, reproduce it with the same parameterised function and print MATCH/MISMATCH; on
     MISMATCH fix the reading before writing. Resolves prose-vs-header conflicts toward the header.
- **Expected effect + why safe:**
  - Base: recovers clusters 1–4, measured at +0.500 on this exact split with 0 tasks broken by
    cand_0001. Not a guess — a pivot of per-task rewards across that run's rollouts.
  - Edit 1 should restore 31628. BOUNDED: grepped all 18 passing traces for `1899,12,30` /
    `toordinal` / `serial_number` → **zero hits**; no passing answer is a serial.
  - Edit 2 targets 43436. I verified arithmetically from the file's own 11 records that the agent's
    written values equal the *overlap* function exactly and differ from the *snapshot* function in
    exactly 5 cells all HIGHER (matching the scorer verbatim), while the filled sibling column H is
    reproduced exactly by snapshot and not by overlap — so the check fires MISMATCH and forces the
    right reading. BOUNDED: it can only confirm a reading that already reproduces the sibling
    column, and fires only when such a column exists.
  - Verified the harness `.format()` contract renders with all six required placeholders intact.
- **Building on prior RESULTS:** used the sibling run's measured per-task matrix as the LEDGER this
  run lacked. Took cand_0001's content (broke nothing) plus cand_0005's four added sections (fixed
  37456, 50768, 80-42). Did **NOT** re-try cand_0002 (broke 2768, 402-43, 51-12, 9569), cand_0003
  (Δ 0; broke 31628, 48527) or cand_0004 (val 0.800).
- **Refuted hypotheses (do not re-test):** (a) a blanket "always use openpyxl / never `to_excel` so
  the workbook is preserved" rule — **13 of 18 passing tasks win via `pandas.to_excel`**; it must
  stay conditional. (b) More prose is not free: cand_0002 and cand_0004 both grew the prompt and
  *lost* val. (c) Restating the snapshot rule as advice does not work — cand_0005 already contained
  it and 43436 still failed; that is why Edit 2 is a printed precondition, not a sentence.
- **High-value clusters still NOT cracked:** 43436 is the long-standing one and Edit 2 is the first
  structural attempt at it (prior attempts were prose). If it still fails, the next lever is to make
  the calibration a *hard gate* — require the MATCH line in the transcript before any write is
  permitted — rather than more explanation.
- **Plateau signal:** none yet for this run (iteration 1). In the sibling run the last three
  candidates were flat-to-negative while the prompt grew, so the lever to prefer is **structural
  preconditions with printed evidence**, not additional explanatory prose.
- **Focus next iteration:** read the RESULT stamp below. If 31628 and 43436 both land, remaining
  headroom is one-off semantic misreadings — resist encoding any specific answer, and consider
  pruning prose that no measured win depends on rather than adding more.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.950 Δ=+0.500 · fixed={227-40, 267-18, 37378, 37456, 39046, 43436, 46897, 48527, 50768, 51-12, 53383, 53647, 54144, 55049, 55979, 56563, 59196, 6698, 7902, 8942, 9569} · broke={31628} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
<!-- cand_0001: ACCEPTED val=0.950 Δ=+0.500 -->

## Iteration cand_0002 — the last two failures share no root cause: one is `max_row` row-inflation on append, one is clause-precedence on answer type

- **Changes I made:**
  1. `prompt.md` §4 **Appending / consolidating** bullet — cluster 80-42: never size an append with
     `ws.max_row`; filter each source's rows on a key column and print `max_row` vs real data count
     per source plus the resulting last row, before writing. Includes the copyable snippet.
  2. `prompt.md` §1(b) — cluster 31628: a **precedence** rule for when two clauses name the same
     answer with different implied types. The clause naming *what to extract* (a date **component**
     → `int`) outranks a later "display the resulting **date**", which is a back-reference and never
     promotes an `int` to a `datetime`. One worked example, invented cells.
  3. `task_template.md` Phase 1 — commit `# ANSWER TYPE: <type>` with the instruction words that fix
     it, before any code assigns a cell (makes edit 2's criterion a precondition of Phase 2).
  4. `task_template.md` Phase 3 — two checklist items: printed `type:` must equal the Phase-1
     committed type; and if rows were appended, the per-source row count must reconcile.
- **Expected effect + why safe:**
  - 80-42: its stdout shows 4998 rows appended where the declared extents total 3998 — exactly 1000
    formatting-only rows from one source, displacing every later row by 1000 and destroying ~24k
    graded cells that were each copied *correctly*. The new printed `max_row` vs `data rows`
    comparison exposes that before the write. BOUNDED: gated on the append/consolidate trigger
    phrases; a subagent audit of all 38 passing traces found 16 that use `max_row` on the write path
    and **all 16 already filter on a key column**, so values are unchanged, and `max_row` is not
    inflated anywhere else in this suite.
  - 31628: the agent derived the right answer and then discarded it — *"'Number of the last day' is
    slightly ambiguous, but 'resulting date' is explicit"* — and wrote a `datetime` where the scorer
    wanted `int`. BOUNDED: fires only when a date component is named; of the 38 passing
    instructions exactly 2 contain component phrases (43436, 8942) and in both the phrase describes a
    filter boundary or an input cell, not the answer, and both already write `int`. The only two
    passing tasks writing a `datetime` (9726, 416-15) name no component, so the rule's explicit
    fallback reproduces them exactly.
  - Edits 3–4 add no computation; they make the type decision and the row reconciliation checkable
    artifacts. Both failures had already *printed* the evidence of their own defect and declared
    success anyway, so the gap was a missing referent to check against, not missing information.
- **Building on prior RESULTS:** kept all of `cand_0001` (ACCEPTED +0.500, broke nothing) untouched;
  both my edits are additive and inside existing sections. `cand_0001`'s Edit 2 (Phase 1b CALIBRATE)
  **worked** — 43436 is in its `fixed` set after failing under every sibling-run candidate — which is
  direct evidence for the lever I reused in edits 3–4: a structural precondition that prints
  evidence, not more prose. I did not re-try sibling `cand_0002` (broke 2768, 402-43, 51-12, 9569),
  `cand_0003` (Δ 0; broke 31628, 48527) or `cand_0004` (val 0.800).
- **Refuted hypotheses (do not re-test):** (a) a blanket "always openpyxl, never `to_excel`" rule —
  13 of the passing tasks win via `pandas.to_excel`. (b) Restating a rule the agent already has:
  `cand_0001`'s prompt *already* said a date **part** is a small integer and 31628 still wrote a
  `datetime` — the missing piece was clause precedence, not emphasis. (c) **New this iteration, found
  before shipping:** asserting "computed last row must not exceed `answer_position`" is *wrong* —
  402-43 passes while writing to row 25 of an `A1:AG10` range. For Sheet-Level tasks the range bounds
  where you may write, not how many rows the answer has. I designed that out; do not add it later.
- **High-value clusters still NOT cracked:** none left unaddressed — only 2 tasks fail and both have a
  fix here. The open question is no longer *which* cluster but whether prose volume is now the binding
  constraint (see plateau).
- **Plateau signal:** not flat yet (last RESULT +0.500), but headroom is down to 2 tasks / 0.050, so
  noise and dilution now dominate. `prompt.md` is 15.1 → 18.0 KB and `task_template.md` 9.2 → 10.6 KB;
  INSIGHTS records that growth *lost* val on this reader (sibling `cand_0002` 13.8 KB → 0.825 vs
  `cand_0001` 8.6 KB → 0.900). I halved both additions after drafting for that reason and shipped no
  speculative third fix. If this is rejected with `broke={}`, read that as length/dilution rather than
  a wrong rule, and the next lever is **subtraction** — prune sections no measured win depends on and
  measure pruning as its own candidate, which this run has never tested.
- **Focus next iteration:** attribute 31628 and 80-42 individually from the RESULT stamp. If 31628
  lands and 80-42 does not, the remaining defect is the interior-blank-row *alignment* rather than the
  count, and the lever is to require printing the first and last appended row of **each** source block
  (so a gap is visible per source, not just in the total). If both land at 1.000, stop adding and test
  pruning.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.925 Δ=-0.025 · fixed={31628, 80-42} · broke={43436, 51-12, 53647} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.
<!-- cand_0002: rejected val=0.925 Δ=-0.025 -->

## Iteration cand_0003 — re-ship cand_0002's two *proven* fixes at near-flat length, and test subtraction for the first time

- **Changes I made:**
  1. `prompt.md` §4 append/consolidate bullet — cluster 80-42: size each source from its declared
     `[data extent]`, never `range(2, ws_src.max_row + 1)`; print `max_row` vs `data rows` per source
     and require the total to equal the sum of the declared extents. Scoped to the **source-read**
     loop with an explicit carve-out that it never governs which rows you write.
  2. `prompt.md` §1(b) — cluster 31628: **replaced** (not stacked on) the old "a date part is a small
     integer" sentence with a precedence rule — the clause carrying the **extraction verb** specifies
     the type; a later "display the resulting date" is a back-reference that says only *where*.
  3. `task_template.md` Phase 1 + Phase 3 — same cluster, structural half: commit `# ANSWER TYPE:`
     before any code assigns a cell, and add a Phase-3 item that nothing in the output may contradict
     it. Plus a "weigh each candidate type once and commit" clause against the 60-line re-litigation
     the trace shows.
  4. `task_template.md`/`prompt.md` — **pruning (new lever this run):** deleted §5's `dropna` bullet
     and demoted §4's `to_excel`-as-co-equal opener to openpyxl-as-default, keeping both
     openpyxl-required conditions verbatim.
- **Expected effect + why safe:**
  - Edit 1 → 80-42. Its stdout gives 4998 rows appended where declared extents total 3998 (start row
    4000 → last row 8997, not 7997): 1000 interior formatting-only rows displaced every later source
    block, destroying ~24k cells each copied *correctly*. BOUNDED: of 25 passing traces using
    `max_row`, only 402-43 has an append trigger and its declared extent equals its printed `max_row`
    (25), so no-op; the only two tasks where `max_row` exceeds the extent (37378, 382-10) do not
    append. The 8 row-for-row-bound passing tasks have no append trigger, and 395-36 (must *emit*
    near-empty rows) is protected by the carve-out sentence.
  - Edits 2+3 → 31628. Scorer: *"1 cell(s) hold datetime where int was expected"*. Not a knowledge
    gap — cand_0001 already had the date-part rule; the trace ranked the clauses wrongly
    (*"'Number of the last day' is slightly ambiguous, but 'resulting date' is explicit"*). BOUNDED:
    exactly 1 of 38 passing instructions names a date component (43436, as a filter boundary; already
    writes `int`), and the only 2 passing tasks writing a `datetime` to a graded cell (416-15, 9726)
    name no component and hit the rule's fallback.
  - Edit 4 is paid for by measurement: `to_excel`, `read_excel` and `dropna` have **0 hits across all
    40 traces** — no trace on this split touches a workbook through pandas. §3's preview-translation
    rules are untouched (3 traces depend on the `i + 2` offset, 2 on the pandas-index rule).
- **Building on prior RESULTS:** cand_0002's stamp says `fixed={31628, 80-42}` — **both its fixes
  worked**; its batch was reverted only because it also broke 43436/51-12/53647. None of those three
  can be *triggered* by either rule (no append, no date component; verified per task), but all three
  need long multi-step reasoning, and its prompt grew +4.3 KB / +18%. So I re-ship the same two
  clusters and treat **length** as the thing to fix: +2.8 KB gross, ~0.9 KB of it recovered by
  deleting verified-dead text. I also dropped cand_0002's `answer_position` row-bound assertion
  entirely and restated the append check purely source-side.
- **Refuted hypotheses (do not re-test):** (a) a blanket "always openpyxl, never `to_excel`" rule —
  would have regressed 13 of 18 passing tasks in the sibling baseline; I demoted the default without
  writing the prohibition. (b) "computed last row must not exceed `answer_position`" — **402-43
  passes writing to row 25 of an `A1:AG10` range**; never re-add. (c) Restating the date-part rule as
  emphasis — cand_0001 contained it and 31628 still failed; the gap is clause precedence.
  (d) **New, caught before shipping:** phrasing the Phase-3 type check as *"the printed `type:` of
  each graded cell equals …"* — 8 passing traces print neither `repr()` nor `type()`, so that wording
  would demand a new print from passing tasks. Reworded to "nothing in the output contradicts it",
  which is a no-op unless the agent contradicts itself.
- **High-value clusters still NOT cracked:** none unaddressed — only 2 tasks fail and both have a fix
  here. The open question is packaging, not diagnosis.
- **Plateau signal:** last RESULT was negative (-0.025) with both intended fixes landing, which points
  at dilution rather than a wrong rule. Hence the lever switch this iteration is **subtraction**, the
  only untried direction in the run. If this is rejected again with the same three tasks in `broke`,
  the hypothesis "added prose displaces reasoning support on this reader" is confirmed and the next
  move is a strictly length-neutral-or-shorter candidate: pay for every addition by deleting more
  than it costs, starting with §2's matrix-orientation passage (1 dependent trace: 50768) and the
  next-row passage (1: 37456).
- **Focus next iteration:** attribute 31628 and 80-42 separately, and read `broke` against total
  length. If both land with `broke={}`, the remaining headroom is 0 and the right move is to stop
  adding and verify stability rather than invent a cluster.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.875 Δ=-0.075 · fixed={31628, 80-42} · broke={395-36, 43436, 48527, 51-12, 9569} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.

# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## The grader reads stored values — `hard_no_recalc` on every task
- **What worked (confirmed):** `score.raw.reward_metric` is `hard_no_recalc` for all 40 val tasks;
  the grader opens the output `data_only=True` and compares stored values. openpyxl writes formulas
  with no cached value, so a formula cell reads back EMPTY and scores 0 however correct it is. The
  output-contract rule "compute in Python, assign the literal, **even when the instruction says
  'formula'**" is the single biggest win available (~11 of 22 failing tasks). Confirmed by the
  sibling run's `cand_0001` (val 0.450 → 0.900, broke nothing).
- **Diagnostic to reuse:** `test_case_results` vs `test_case_results_no_recalc` in `score.raw`
  separates "logic wrong" from "artifact wrong". 7 tasks showed `recalc=[1], no_recalc=[0]` —
  correct formula logic, zero score. Always print both arrays before theorising.
- **What didn't:** nothing here; the risk is the reverse — the task instructions themselves ask for
  "a formula", which is what baits the agent into breaking the contract.

## Preserve-the-workbook must stay CONDITIONAL
- **What didn't (confirmed):** a blanket "always use openpyxl + `wb.save`, never `to_excel`" rule
  would regress **13 of the 18 passing tasks**, which win via `pandas.to_excel`. The clobbering
  cluster (80-42, 227-40, 39046, 48527) is real, but the fix must be scoped to the two conditions
  where a rebuild loses data — appending/consolidating, and a sheet holding content the DataFrame
  does not carry.
- **Promising:** the off-by-one half of that cluster is separable — `pd.read_excel` consumes Excel
  row 1 as the header, so df row `i` is Excel row `i + 2`. 227-40 failed purely on this.

## Prose the agent already has is not a fix — make it a printed precondition
- **What didn't (confirmed):** the sibling run's `cand_0005` prompt already contained the
  snapshot-vs-overlap rule as advice, and task 43436 still failed under it (and under every other
  candidate). Restating a rule the agent skips changes nothing.
- **Promising but not yet tried (this iteration's Edit 2):** when a filled column outside the target
  names the **same quantity at a different parameter** (`Open as of today` beside `Open by end of
  May`), it is a worked example of the requested function. Requiring the agent to reproduce it and
  print MATCH/MISMATCH *before* writing turns the rule into a check it cannot skip. Verified
  offline: the snapshot function reproduces that column exactly, overlap does not, and the agent's
  overlap answer differs from expected in exactly the 5 cells the scorer flagged.

## Adding prose has a cost
- **What didn't (confirmed):** sibling-run `cand_0002` (13.8 KB prompt) scored 0.825 and `cand_0004`
  0.800, both below `cand_0001`'s 8.6 KB / 0.900. Prompt growth without measured attribution loses
  val on this reader (`gemma-4-31B-it`, weaker on long context). Prefer restructuring over appending.

## `answer_position` is NOT an assertion about how many rows the answer has
- **What didn't (confirmed by cand_0001's RESULT):** task **402-43 scores 1.0 while writing to row 25
  of an `answer_position` of `'Sheet2'!A1:AG10`** — it overshoots the range by 15 rows and is still
  graded correct. So any rule of the form "if your last written row exceeds the range's last row, your
  row count is wrong" is **false** and would tell a passing task to corrupt its own answer. For
  Sheet-Level Manipulation the range bounds *where you may write*, not the answer's extent. Three more
  appending tasks (395-36, 463-17, 227-40) land *exactly* on their last row, so a "near the end looks
  suspicious" heuristic false-fires on all three too. Designed out of cand_0002 before shipping; never
  re-add it.
- **Promising:** the safe substitute is source-side — compare each source sheet's `max_row` against its
  real data-row count. That is a statement about the *input*, needs no knowledge of the answer's size,
  and cannot fire on 402-43.

## `ws.max_row` over-reports, and on an append that misaligns everything downstream
- **What didn't (confirmed by cand_0001's RESULT, task 80-42):** sizing an append with
  `range(2, ws_src.max_row + 1)` appended 4998 rows where the declared extents total 3998 — one source
  carried exactly 1000 formatting-only rows. The damage is not junk at the bottom: the 1000 blanks are
  *interior*, so every later source block sat 1000 rows too low and ~24k graded cells were compared
  against the wrong record **even though every value was copied correctly**. The preview's
  `[data extent: rows 1-N]` is measured on real data and disagreed with `max_row`; it is the number to
  trust.
- **What worked (safe scoping, from the cand_0002 audit):** 16 of the 38 passing tasks use `max_row` on
  the write path and **all 16 already guard with a None/truthiness test on a key column** — so a
  "filter empty source rows" rule is a no-op on their values. Keep it on the **source-read** loop only:
  7 passing tasks (53647, 37378, 48620, 2768, 9569, 48921, 59595) bind graded output row-for-row to the
  source, and 395-36 must *emit* near-empty rows, so a skip-empty rule reaching the write loop would
  misalign or truncate them. 48620 is the canary — its answer depends on Nth-occurrence indexing over
  column A, which any dropped source row shifts.

## A restated rule loses to a competing clause — state PRECEDENCE, not the rule again
- **What didn't (confirmed by cand_0001's RESULT, task 31628):** `cand_0001`'s prompt already said a
  date **part** is "that component as a small integer", and the agent still wrote a `datetime` and
  scored 0 (*"1 cell(s) hold datetime where int was expected"*). Its own reasoning shows why: it found
  both readings and then ranked them wrongly — *"'Number of the last day' is slightly ambiguous, but
  'resulting date' is explicit."* The rule was present; what was missing was a way to **rank two
  clauses of the same instruction**. These instructions are user-written and routinely restate the same
  answer a clause later in looser words that imply a different type.
- **Promising (cand_0002's edit):** state precedence explicitly — the clause naming *what to extract*
  wins; a later "display the resulting date" / "show the result" is a back-reference that decides
  nothing. Verified BOUNDED: only 2 of 38 passing instructions contain a date-component phrase (43436,
  8942) and in both it describes a filter boundary or an input cell rather than the answer; the only two
  passing tasks writing a `datetime` (9726, 416-15) name no component and hit the rule's fallback.
- **General form worth reusing:** when a trace shows the agent *reaching* the correct reading and then
  abandoning it, the gap is never knowledge — it is a missing tie-break, or a missing referent to check
  the result against. Both of cand_0002's failures had already **printed** the evidence of their own
  defect and declared success; what they lacked was something to compare that printout to.

# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001
- **Strategy tried:** before writing anything, I searched the project dir for *any* already-measured
  signal rather than trusting the empty `LEDGER.md`/`RUNMAP.md`. That found
  `reused_seed_run/run_suite/` — a completed run on the identical seed baseline, identical val split
  and identical reader model, with per-task rollouts for 5 scored candidates. Pivoting reward per
  task per candidate converted what the instructions framed as a blank-slate guess into an
  attribution problem: I could see exactly which prose fixed which task and which broke which. This
  was by far the highest-leverage 20 minutes of the iteration and it should be the default first move
  on any "empty seed" iteration.
- **Where the framing misled me initially:** "EMPTY SEED — create the capability from scratch"
  reads as an instruction to *author* content, and the natural failure mode is to write a fresh
  prompt from the traces and discard a measured +0.500 that already exists on disk. Empty capability
  dir ≠ no prior evidence.
- **Subagent fan-out:** four parallel read-only `Explore` agents (three failure groups + one
  dedicated to surveying the 18 *passing* tasks). The passing-task survey was the most valuable and
  is the one I would always repeat: it pre-empted a blanket "always use openpyxl" rule that would
  have regressed 13 of 18 passing tasks. Diagnosing what must NOT change deserves a whole subagent,
  not a footnote.
- **Subagents disagree; data does not.** Two agents returned opposite conclusions on whether the
  grader recalculates formulas. Resolving it from `score.raw.reward_metric` + the two result arrays
  took one command. Treat a subagent's report as a hypothesis to check, never as a measurement.
- **Plateau/stall signal:** none in this run yet (iteration 1). But the sibling run plateaued at
  0.900–0.950 across its last three candidates while the prompt grew 8.6 KB → 15 KB, with two of
  them *losing* val. Read that as: on this reader, added prose has negative expected value once the
  big contract rules are in place; the productive lever is structural (an ordered precondition that
  prints evidence) rather than explanatory.
- **What to try next iteration:** (1) read the RESULT stamp and attribute 31628 / 43436 individually.
  (2) If 43436 still fails, escalate Phase 1b from "do this check" to a hard gate — no write
  permitted until the MATCH line exists. (3) Consider *pruning* prompt sections no measured win
  depends on, and measure that as its own candidate; the run has never tested subtraction.

## Iteration cand_0002
- **Strategy tried:** with only 2 failing tasks left (LEDGER row 1: 0.950, 38/40), the search problem
  inverted. At 22 failures the job was *finding* clusters; at 2 it is *not damaging the 38*. So I spent
  most of the iteration on blast radius rather than diagnosis — diagnosis took two trace reads and one
  arithmetic check, and the audit of what must not change took the rest.
- **The instructions' framing fought the situation, and I think correctly resisting it was right.**
  "Make AS MANY fixes as you can — a timid one- or two-edit iteration is an under-used iteration" is
  sound advice at 22 failures and actively harmful at 2: there is no third cluster, so a third edit
  could only be speculative, and the expected value of a speculative edit against 38 passing tasks is
  negative. I shipped 4 edits covering exactly the 2 real clusters and said so explicitly. **A future
  iteration at low headroom should read "breadth" as "cover every real cluster", not "produce N edits".**
- **The highest-value move was asking the subagent for per-task verdicts, not a summary.** Requiring
  WOULD-CHANGE / NO-CHANGE / RULE-DOES-NOT-FIRE *per task id, with quoted evidence* is what surfaced
  the 402-43 hazard: my drafted bound check ("appended last row must not exceed `answer_position`")
  would have told a **currently-passing** task its correct answer was a row-count error. A prose
  summary would have said "looks safe". That one finding justified the whole audit — and it is the
  second time in this run that a subagent aimed at the *passing* set paid for itself.
- **Re-derive the subagent's decisive numbers.** Per last iteration's lesson I re-checked the two facts
  the edits rest on directly from the traces (3998 declared rows vs 4998 appended; the scorer's
  "datetime where int was expected"). Both held. The subagent's *verdicts* were where the value was;
  its arithmetic I did not need to trust.
- **Plateau/stall signal:** none in the measured record yet, but the *mechanism* has changed: at 0.050
  remaining headroom, per-task noise and prompt dilution are now comparable to the achievable gain.
  Prose volume is the one variable that has moved val negatively in the sibling run while looking free.
  I halved both drafted additions after writing them; that self-editing pass should be a standing step,
  not an afterthought.
- **What to try next iteration:** (1) attribute 31628 / 80-42 separately from the RESULT stamp — they
  are independent, so a partial accept is informative. (2) If this is rejected with `broke={}`, stop
  treating it as a wrong-rule problem and **test subtraction**: prune prose no measured win depends on
  and measure it as its own candidate. This run has never tested removing anything, and it is the only
  untried direction left. (3) Never re-add the `answer_position` row-bound assertion (refuted above).

# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## Iteration cand_0001 (SpreadsheetBench, empty-seed)

1. **An "empty seed" iteration should be told whether prior measured evidence exists.** My working
   dir had an empty `LEDGER.md`, an empty `RUNMAP.md`, no `prior_iterations/` and an empty
   `rejected.jsonl`, and INSTRUCTIONS said "create the capability from scratch". Meanwhile the
   project directory contained `reused_seed_run/run_suite/` — a *completed* run on the identical seed
   baseline, identical val split and identical reader model, with five scored candidates and full
   per-task rollouts, one of them measured at val 0.950 / test 0.771. Had I followed the framing
   literally and authored fresh prose from the traces, I would have discarded a measured +0.500. Two
   fixes: (a) when a run reuses a seed whose evaluation already exists, surface that path in
   `RUNMAP.md`/`LEDGER.md` explicitly as "measured evidence for this baseline lives here"; (b) soften
   "create from scratch" to "the capability *files* are empty — check for prior measured runs on this
   baseline first".

2. **`LEDGER.md`'s "never re-introduce a change that broke a task" is unusable at iteration 1**, yet
   it is stated as a primary safety check. The equivalent evidence existed but in a location the
   instructions never mention. Consider having the framework pre-populate the ledger from any reused
   run's `history.jsonl` / `rejected.jsonl`.

3. **The per-task `broke`/`fixed` pivot should be a provided tool, not a thing each optimizer
   re-derives.** The single most decisive artifact I built was a task × candidate reward matrix from
   `rollouts/val/<task>__<cand>__t0.json`. Every iteration that inherits scored rollouts needs
   exactly this. A `scripts/pivot.py` (or a `RUNMAP.md` section rendering it) would save each
   iteration the rediscovery and make regression attribution the default rather than an initiative.

4. **The capability file list should name the files even when they are empty.** INSTRUCTIONS said the
   edit space is `prompt.md` + `task_template.md`, but only a zero-byte `prompt.md` existed —
   `task_template.md` was absent, so it was unclear whether creating it was in scope or whether the
   harness would even read it. I confirmed the contract only by reading a sibling run's candidate.
   Shipping a commented stub of each expected file (with the load-bearing placeholders) in an
   empty-seed dir would remove that ambiguity, which matters because a wrong guess about the
   placeholders zeroes all 40 tasks.

5. **Useful scorer behaviour worth documenting for prose-capability tasks:** this adapter exposes both
   `test_case_results` and `test_case_results_no_recalc` plus `reward_metric`. That pair cleanly
   separates "the agent's logic was wrong" from "the agent's artifact was wrong" and pointed
   immediately at the largest cluster (7 tasks with correct formula logic scored 0). The diagnose
   skill should tell optimizers to look for such paired metrics — it is a much stronger signal than
   the prose feedback string.

files.text:
# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

EMPTY SEED iteration: `prompt.md` was 0 bytes and `task_template.md` did not exist. The agent ran
with only the adapter's built-in task framing, which told it *"once that file exists, you are
done"* — the single most damaging line in the baseline.

## Decisive discovery: measured evidence already existed for this exact baseline

`LEDGER.md` / `RUNMAP.md` / `rejected.jsonl` were all empty (iteration 1 of this run), so this
looked like a blank slate. It is not. The project dir contains a **sibling completed run**,
`reused_seed_run/run_suite/`, on the **same seed baseline and the same val split** — identical
val 0.450 and the identical 18-task passing set — with full per-task rollouts, candidate files,
`history.jsonl` and `rejected.jsonl`. I confirmed the reader model is identical in both runs
(`litellm_proxy/rits/google/gemma-4-31B-it`), so those measurements transfer.

Pivoting per-task reward across its candidates (`rollouts/val/<task>__<cand>__t0.json`):

| candidate | val | measured outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| seed | 0.450 | 18/40 |
| cand_0001 | **0.900** | fixed 18 tasks, **broke 0** |
| cand_0002 | 0.825 | rejected (broke 2768, 402-43, 51-12, 9569) |
| cand_0003 | 0.900 | rejected (Δ 0; broke 31628, 48527) |
| cand_0004 | 0.800 | rejected |
| cand_0005 | **0.950** | = cand_0001 + 4 sections; fixed 37456/50768/80-42, **broke 31628** |

Its accepted final scored **0.771 on held-out test**, so that prose generalizes rather than
overfitting the val split. Rebuilding this content from scratch and hoping to rediscover it would
have thrown away a measured +0.500. So the base of this candidate is `cand_0005`'s two files,
and my own work is the two edits below: repair its one measured regression, and crack the one
cluster no candidate ever fixed.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Formula written instead of value | 37378, 46897, 53383, 55049, 6698, 7902, 8942 (+4 more) | `reward_metric=hard_no_recalc` on all 40 tasks: grader reads stored values, never recalculates. All 7 have `recalc=[1], no_recalc=[0]` — logic already right | KNOWLEDGE | output contract (base) |
| 2 | Never inspects the real file | 267-18, 55979, 50768, 43436, 59196 (5 of 5 checked) | Treats the truncated prompt preview as ground truth; sandbox used write-only. Not one trace printed a cell value | BEHAVIORAL | ordered procedure (base) |
| 3 | No-op retry loop | 10 failing + 10 passing tasks | Reads `[Code executed successfully with no output]` as "not done yet"; re-emits byte-identical block ~28× to turn 30. Baseline framing *"once that file exists, you are done"* actively discouraged verifying | BEHAVIORAL | stop-condition + verify phase (base) |
| 4 | Destructive `to_excel` rebuild | 80-42, 227-40, 39046, 48527, 50768 | `read_excel`+`to_excel` rewrites the sheet, destroying untouched cells/sheets/formatting; default header also shifts rows by one | KNOWLEDGE | conditional rule (base) |
| 5 | Prose/header semantic mismatch | **43436** | Instruction's prose paraphrase describes *overlap with the period*; the graded column's header says *snapshot at the boundary*. Agent followed the prose | BEHAVIORAL | **calibration step (MY EDIT 2)** |
| 6 | Date → Excel serial | **31628** (regression) | "as a static number" misread as "the 45301-style serial"; overrode an already-correct answer | KNOWLEDGE | **typed-value rule (MY EDIT 1)** |

Clusters 1–4 are covered by the measured-0.900/0.950 base. Clusters 5 and 6 are mine.

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit)
| cluster | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6 / 31628 | add a sourced rule to the output contract (skill lever 4 + 8) | `prompt.md` §1(b) | States that "as a static number" / "as a value not a formula" / "hard-code it" all describe *storage form* (literal vs formula), never a re-encoding of a date as a serial; and that a request for a date *part* is that component as a small int. Names the exact anti-pattern `(d - datetime(1899,12,30)).days`. General: it is a fact about this benchmark's whole date class, no task id or answer | YES — bounded |
| 5 / 43436 | ordered procedure, made a precondition (skill lever 6 + the SKIPPED-STEP lever) | `task_template.md` new **Phase 1b** | When a column just outside the target is already filled and its header names the **same quantity at a different parameter**, it is a worked example of the function being asked for. The agent must parameterise its reading, reproduce that column, and print MATCH/MISMATCH **before writing**. Resolves prose-vs-header conflicts in favour of the header. General: describes a structural property of the file, not a task | YES — bounded, additive |

Both are ADDITIVE and condition-guarded. Neither loosens a permission nor alters a global
decision rule. I did NOT re-try the edits from cand_0002/0003/0004, which measurement showed
regressed (2768, 402-43, 51-12, 9569, 31628, 48527).

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change)

- **EDIT 1 — trace `31628__cand_0005`:** agent got `B1 = 10` (correct, `.day`), then reasoned *"a
  date 'as a number' is its serial number"*, recomputed `(2024-01-10 − 1899-12-30).days = 45301`,
  and overwrote its own right answer; scorer: *"1 cell(s) hold a number HIGHER than expected"*.
  Under `cand_0001` (no such reasoning available) the same task scored 1.0 with `10`. The new rule
  names that exact conversion as never-an-answer, so the agent keeps `.day`. **Blast radius
  (BOUNDED):** grepped all 18 passing traces for `1899,12,30` / `toordinal` / `serial_number` —
  **zero hits**, so no passing task's winning answer is a serial. Fires only on date-to-number.
- **EDIT 2 — trace `43436__cand_0005`:** agent wrote *"a record is open if it was created on or
  before the last day and was not yet closed or closed on or after the first day — this 'overlap'
  logic was applied"*. I re-derived both readings from the file's own 11 records in Python:
  its written values `A[1,2,2] B[4,4,4] C[2,2,2] D[1,0,0] E[0,0,1]` equal the **overlap** function
  exactly, and differ from the **snapshot** function in exactly **5 cells, all HIGHER** — matching
  the scorer verbatim (*"5 of 15 … hold a number HIGHER than expected"*). Critically, the filled
  sibling column H (`Open as of today`, `A=1 B=2 C=1 D=0 E=1`) is reproduced **exactly** by the
  snapshot function and **not** by overlap. So the calibration check would have printed MISMATCH
  before writing and forced the correct reading. This is the verification the base prompt's
  existing snapshot *advice* lacked — the rule was already there in prose (`cand_0005` §2) and the
  agent skipped it, which is why this edit is STRUCTURE (a precondition with a printed
  MATCH/MISMATCH gate), not another sentence. **Blast radius (BOUNDED):** the check only ever
  *confirms* a reading that already reproduces the sibling column; it cannot change a reading that
  matches. It fires only when such a filled same-quantity-different-parameter column exists.
- **Contract safety (both files):** simulated the harness's `.format()` — all six required
  placeholders (`{instruction}` `{spreadsheet_path}` `{spreadsheet_content}` `{instruction_type}`
  `{answer_position}` `{output_path}`) plus `{max_turns}` substitute cleanly, no stray single
  braces, no invented placeholders. This was worth checking explicitly: breaking it zeroes all 40.

## Process & features used
- **Parallel fan-out (Phase 1):** four read-only `Explore` subagents diagnosed in parallel —
  formula/value + error-text group; clobbering/empty-target group; the 18 passing tasks as an
  explicit blast-radius survey; and the wrong-computed-value group. Main agent deduped into the 6
  clusters above. The passing-task subagent produced the most valuable result: it found that **13
  of 18 passing tasks depend on `pandas.to_excel`**, so a blanket "always use openpyxl to preserve
  the workbook" rule — tempting from the clobbering cluster — would have regressed 13 tasks. The
  base prompt's conditional phrasing is correct and I left it alone.
- Two subagents disagreed on whether the grader recalculates. I resolved it from data rather than
  accepting either: `score.raw.reward_metric` is `hard_no_recalc` on all 40 tasks, and the
  `test_case_results` vs `test_case_results_no_recalc` split proves 7 tasks had correct formula
  logic scored zero. Worth recording — an agent's report is a hypothesis, not a measurement.
- Serial implementation for the two edits: both are small and interacting, and I already had the
  measured attribution, so worktree fan-out would have cost more than it saved.
- **Prior iterations read:** `./prior_iterations/` and `RUNMAP.md` are empty. The real prior work
  is `reused_seed_run/run_suite/` (read-only), mined as described above. I made **no** edit to any
  adapter/harness/scorer/benchmark file; the sibling run was used only as evidence.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- The §1 output contract "a formula is not an answer — write the computed literal", including the
  *"even when the instruction says 'formula'"* clause. This is the single biggest measured win
  (~11 tasks) and the instructions actively bait the agent into breaking it.
- The **conditional** phrasing of the preserve-the-workbook rule. Do **not** promote it to a
  blanket openpyxl mandate: 13 of 18 passing tasks win via `pandas.to_excel`.
- The Phase 3 stop condition ("if every check passes, reply with no code block; do not re-send
  working code"). 20 of 40 seed tasks burned ~28 rounds re-emitting identical blocks.
- The explicit "reply with **no code block** when done" wording — that, not the file's existence,
  is what terminates the loop.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- **No environment fault found.** Every trace executed its code and produced a file; failures are
  genuine capability failures. No infra diagnosis to hand back.
- **9569 / 80-42 / 37456 / 50768** — already fixed by base content at their measured 0.950; adding
  more prose risks the length/attention regression seen in cand_0002 and cand_0004.
- **Did not chase a 40/40.** The remaining headroom sits in one-off semantic misreadings where the
  only "fix" would be to encode a specific task's answer — that overfits and the held-out gate
  punishes it. I kept every edit to a general, file-structural property.
